utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Latifi. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your examination by Mr. Visnjic will now continue. Please remember that the solemn declaration which you made at the very beginning of your evidence continues to apply to that evidence today also. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Latifi.

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi, yesterday we left off when we were discussing the kidnapping of Ymer Xhafiqi. Could we please have on e-court D140 page 2. Mr. Latifi, I'll try to refresh your memory by reading a portion of the exhibit. This is another Kosovo verification mission report. "Albanian workers [Previous translation continues] ... police as a civil servant was kidnapped in the village of Pirana this morning. According to police sources he was not connected with operational matters. The KLA have indirectly confirmed their involvement in the matter although at this stage the reasons for the abductions are still unclear." [Interpretation] Mr. Latifi, does this refresh your recollection concerning the fact that the KLA was involved in the abduction of Rahim Latifi [sic] after all?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that I had heard that he was kidnapped but I didn't know who kidnapped him. How can I refresh my recollection because -- when I did not hear about this event and I told you that I did not hear who kidnapped him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just a clarification. I asked about two abductions yesterday, of the witness. One was a person by the name of Hajer Tarjani and that took place in 1998 during the summer. The other person that we mentioned just a second ago, Ymer Xhafiqi, was kidnapped on the 9th of March 1999. According to witness statements, both bodies were found at a later stage, but people were dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Latifi, let us move on to an area from the Milosevic case. During the cross-examination there, at page 3649 to 3652, you provided answers concerning several incidents which resulted in the murders of some people, and according to Milosevic's allegations, these murders were committed by the KLA. My question is this: When being proofed for this testimony, did you go through your testimony in the Milosevic case again and do you have anything to add concerning your replies provided about the murders of these people which according to the allegations were committed by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regard to the first case, Hajer Tarjani was found, so his body was found, while Ymer Xhafiqi has not been found yet. With regard to the second case, that the KLA is alleged to have kidnapped them, you are saying that. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Latifi. I wanted to know this. While testifying in Milosevic, he asked a series of questions of you, specifying the names of persons allegedly killed by the KLA and this does not comprise the two men from your village. I don't know whether you can recollect that, but should it be necessary, I can assist you with that. Do you remember Milosevic having asked you about the murders of both Serbs and Albanians which took place in the vicinity of your village or rather in its general area?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember vaguely.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that most of those murders, apart from one, you stated that you were not familiar or rather that you didn't know of those murders?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of those murders but you're mentioning one person. What case is that, according to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: You were able to or rather you heard of the murder of Zvesdal Tasic. As for the other Serbs and Albanians that had been killed, you said you didn't know about that. Very well. In the Milosevic case, on page 3649, you also stated you didn't know anything about the existence of the KLA in the area of Pirana, Retimlje and Randobrava; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that there was no KLA in Pirana. In Randobrava, I did not see any KLA. I don't think I spoke anything about Reti and there was no KLA in Serbica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: You didn't mention that but Milosevic asked you this at page 3649.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 3694.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: On that same page you stated, and this is at page 3694, line 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Hold on. The Milosevic transcript that we have doesn't go to page 3694.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think the interpreter's correction got wrong in the transcript. It's 3649.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I can't see it on 3649.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The question is at 3648.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I mixed up the numbers. 3649, the actual answer I was looking for is at page 3649, line 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi, I wanted to ask you the following: Did you know that as regards the territory of Randobrava and Pirana villages, there was a KLA unit that was tasked with that area comprising some 50 to 70 members? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear about that and I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did you know that the person commanding the unit was Xhavid Elshani who was also from the village of Pirana?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no links with the KLA. I said that in my statement as well. As regards Xhavid Elshani, I did not know or I was not aware that he was some kind of a leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: How far is Randobrava from your village?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: About five kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did your co-villagers hesitate to go to Randobrava for security reasons? This was up until the 24th of March 1999.

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I did not ask anyone about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did you yourself go to Randobrava?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My sister is married there so I went to visit her.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did you know that one of the roads or paths used by the KLA was the one going via the villages of Opterusha, Mamusha, Pirana, Krusha e Madhe and the border with Albania? Was this a regular route used by the KLA for supply and manning of its units? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about the road. Maybe they did these things at night but I didn't see anything. My house is at the entrance of the village. I don't know about these things, this corridor that you're mentioning. It was none of my business.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi, yesterday at page 85, in lines 23 through 25, you stated, "Whenever we saw forces in movement, for example during the Orahovac offensive, we would leave our houses for periods of up to 10 days." My question concerning this is the following: Did you know that the inhabitants of your village, during 1999, before the 24th of March, that is, would leave the village in great numbers?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the Orahovac offensive I stayed at home. My family did not leave. I didn't think it was necessary for us to leave. Some left for security reasons because the forces behaved so badly, the military and police forces, that they instilled fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi, I don't know whether you mentioned to notice but I asked you about 1999. The Orahovac offensive took place in 1998. Therefore my question is whether during 1999, including January, February and March, before the 24th of March, that is, was there any mass movement of the inhabitants of your village or, rather, out of your village? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this period, I don't think I saw people leaving.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you move on, Mr. Visnjic, just to clarify the last point. You did say yesterday that you were dealing with a different point but you did say that there were periods when you did not stay in your own home, and an example you gave was being away for 10 days if you saw forces moving, for example during the Orahovac offensive. Now, was that answer wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1998, during the Orahovac offensive, we moved our families for about 10 days, but not outside the village, while with regard to January, February and March 1999, I don't think I said anything about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi, in your village, there was a branch of the LDK party back in 1999. That branch was headed by a teacher from your village, am I correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: While we are on the subject of the teacher, would I be correct in saying that in your village, there was an elementary school used on an equal footing by the Serbian and Albanian students up until the beginning of the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And there were 837 Albanian students in 32 classrooms, plus 42 teachers and 37 Serb students with their eight teachers, and they used the classrooms that were left. Does that more or less tally with what you know about that elementary school?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact figures but I know that there were -- there was a great number of pupils. I don't know how many classes and so on but I know that there were eight grades. I did not work there so I couldn't know how many students or how many teachers were in the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand. Could we please get Exhibit D138 ready? Mr. Latifi, this is yet another report of the European Community Monitoring Mission, 3D138. And I wanted to read out parts of that report, in which the president of the local LDK notifies the monitoring mission that over 80 per cent of the population - this is on page 2, paragraph 3 - over 80 per cent of the population -- 85 per cent of the population, fled last Saturday, fled the village, and then subsequently all of them returned. The same person, in another exhibit, Exhibit 141, notified the KVM that over 60 per cent of the women and children left Pirana on the 9th of March. So now we have two dates, the 27th of February and the 9th of March. Do you know of a reason as to why the LDK president would misinform the monitoring mission as regards the majority of the population having left the village?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he would misinform or not. It's his problem. He was a leader. As far as I know, my family did not leave. My house is in the outskirts of the village and maybe I didn't notice the other people but he was more informed than me about these matters, of course, but there was panic all the time; I can tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I apologise, there seems to be something that needs to be corrected in the transcript. At page 8, line 2 it should read the 27th of February and the 9th of March. You are telling me now that on both these dates there was panic in your village. Did I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said there was panic all the time, non-stop, because every time the forces moved, people were frightened. I was frightened as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi, was it perhaps because, as it is stated in this report in paragraph 3.2, was it because there was a claim that your village was at the crossroads used by the KLA, one of the roads being from the border to Opterusha and the other one being the one used by the police to patrol, this being the Prizren Gjakova road? Is your village in a place where there was constant contact between the police and the KLA where there were ongoing incidents of the KLA attacking the police? Was that the reason, sir?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't think that is the reason. Our village is on the crossroad that links the road, Prizren Gjakova and the other road that goes to Mamusha but the forces were in constant movement there. They went to Gjakova to Orahovac, and with every movement of the forces, we felt this panic, but I did not see any KLA forces moving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, is that not actually consistent with what the report says?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honour. In paragraph 3.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, it is the movement of the MUP forces that seems to have caused the fleeing of the villagers.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, Your Honour, there is also mention of the road used by the KLA, paragraph 3.2 in the third line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I appreciate that but I don't read into this report a statement that it's activity by the KLA that's causing people to move from the village, which I presume is the point you're trying to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is precisely what I was asking the witness. Also, Your Honour, in paragraph 2.2, there is a mention of the hesitation of the villagers to travel towards the village of Randobrava or rather the reluctance of the villagers.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi, in the Milosevic case at page 3644, you stated that you saw Prizren being bombed whilst you were in Serbica. My question is this: Did you see the bombing of your village of Pirana while you were in Serbica?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prizren was not bombed. The army barracks, we learned that they were bombed by NATO while on the 24th and 25th of March, Randobrava, Reti, were shelled from Serbica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: No, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say what you quoted me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Since you spent about a month in Serbica, during that one month, did you see that the village -- your village or the area around your village was bombed?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On those dates that I mentioned, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did you know that up until the 1st of June 1999, NATO attacked your village or its environs on 34 occasions?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 24th and up until the 26th of April, I was there. During this time, I did not see any bombing in our area, in the villages around Pirana.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Tell me just one thing: How far is Serbica from Pirana?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 2 and a half to three kilometres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think just to be clear about one question, Mr. Visnjic, at line 7 of page 10, you asked during that one month in Serbica, did you see that the village, your village or the area around your village was bombed? Now, the answer was on these dates that I mentioned, yes. Now if that's a reference to NATO bombing, it's not consistent with the rest of the evidence. It may be it's not in fact a reference to NATO bombing at all. Mr. Latifi, just to clear this question, while you were in Serbica, did you personally see any bombing of any part of Prizren or Pirana?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By whom? By the Serb police and military forces or by NATO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: By NATO air forces.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no bombing. Later on I learned that the military barracks were bombed at Prizren.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You told us what you heard. I'm concerned at the moment to know what you saw and you saw no bombing by NATO forces of any part of Prizren or Pirana?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I'm sure there was no bombing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Aleksic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have do have some questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Latifi. My name is Djuro Cepic. I'm one of the attorneys at law on the Defence team of General Lazarevic. Yesterday in the course of your testimony you stated that the minaret of the mosque was destroyed on the 25th of March 1999. Would I be right if I said that you did not see the minaret being destroyed?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 24th of March, a shell fell at the mosque, and with anti-aircraft Pragas, there was shelling from the bridge. On the 28th of March, mines were laid at 8.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you a specific question and I would appreciate a specific answer. The specific question is: Did you see the destruction of the minaret, yes or no? Did you witness it?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning, we saw it, but when it was mined, we didn't. However, we heard the detonation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And I would like a specific answer. Right. Thank you. However, you gave a statement, Mr. Latifi, in 1999, and on page 2 in the last paragraph, you state the following: "Approximately the same time Serbs started shelling the village, but luckily, there was no damage or people killed." I repeat, "Luckily there was no damage or anyone killed." How come that seven years later, seven years after the event and seven years after this statement you had changed this statement? Did anyone suggest to you what you should be saying before this Court, Mr. Latifi?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you think, not me. And if the interpreters could be a little bit louder.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you know Hyseni Fatmir, a resident of your village?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fatmir?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Maybe it would refresh your memory if I said that it was a person who was disarmed together with Mr. Selimi on the 1st of February 1999 in the basement or rather in the cellars of Kosovo Wine company. That's something that my colleague Mr. Visnjic mentioned.

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know your own co-villager, Bytyqi Xhemail?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Xhemail Bytyqi or Jemile? Is it Chimi rather than Xhemail.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Xhemail?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is no Jemile.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is there anyone with a similar name?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a Xhemail Bytyqi but not Jemile Bytyqi. This is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Before I continue, line 25, page 12, we do not have the witness's answer on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is your recollection of his answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. That makes the correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This person that you mentioned and corrected my pronunciation of his name, do you know that he was arrested on the 4th of January 1999 on charges of terrorism by the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Xhemail is an uncle from my father's side but I never heard of this thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi, you gave an additional statement to my learned friend, Mr. Marcussen on the 9th of October, 2006; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In that interview, in paragraph 10, it is stated that in the last days of March, 1999, you toured a number of villages looking for your sister. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I suppose those are the villages of Randobrava, lower Retimlje, Velika Krusa, is that correct that those were the villages you toured looking for your sister?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And further on, it is stated in this statement that the young men you mentioned are considered by you to be members of the KLA, they wore uniforms and carried weapons. Isn't it correct that you encountered those young men on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I encountered young men, that is true, but they were in civilian clothes and they were not armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Nonetheless, Mr. Latifi, quite the contrary is stated here, namely that they were wearing uniforms and they were armed. And those are your words, Mr. Latifi.

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said was that in Randobrava village, in the evening, I came across two persons who were armed, but the others that I saw, they were unarmed. They were in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The two ones who were armed, they were wearing uniforms of the so-called KLA, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for your answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic. Mr. Marcussen?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, I don't have any issue with what my learned friend just said. I just wanted to point out that it was said that a statement was given by the witness on the 9th of October. What we have disclosed is a supplemental information sheet that was as a result of the proofing and I drafted that based on the video proofing we had tried to conduct. Just so the record is clear. That's what the witness said but it's technically not a statement that he has signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I do have some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Our calculations indicate that already an hour has been exhausted in cross-examination. Are you going to be long?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I need at least 15, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just give us a moment, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think there is maybe a lesson to be learned from this particular cross-examination about prioritising the issues. The problem I think is that Mr. Visnjic has spent a lot of time on matters which undoubtedly are relevant to the case and are of some importance but which perhaps might be better explored and more productively explored with other witnesses than with a witness who can't speak to personal knowledge of documents that are being placed in front of him. We recognise, however, Mr. Lukic, that you've got a quite separate interest and therefore we will not prevent you from cross-examining, but perhaps this illustrates the need for better coordination where possible among the Defence and an indication to the Bench in advance when it's anticipated that it's likely that the time normally expected for such cross-examination will be exceeded. But please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Latifi, my name is Branko Lukic. I will try to go through my questions that I have prepared as quickly as possible. You speak of the rifles that Serb forces used to set houses on fire. Can you tell us exactly what kind of rifles they were?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To what I could see, it resembled a pistol, and this is approximately a description because I saw it from far. He was carrying it in his hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you saw the army and the police, you activated your group in charge of the evacuation of the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not organise any group.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did some villagers set out to Mamusha and others to Donja Serbica?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before that, you did have an evacuation plan for the village, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not aware of any plan of this kind. I was not informed about the existence of such a plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On page -- English version second page, last paragraph, Albanian version, page 2, last paragraph, you say, "By then we had an evacuation group that we organised ourselves so as to know what to do just in case." Is that a misrepresentation of your statement?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not a misinterpretation of my statement. I was not involved in the organisation of that group. It was a group of five or six people who were monitoring the situation and what was going on in the villages around us, and the movements of the Serb forces, Serb military and police forces. They first noticed that there was an open corridor in the direction of Mamusha but later on, that route was blocked.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You went to Donja Serbica and that is in fact the village closest to yours, next door to Pirana?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's closer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say that policemen, around 70 of them, came to Donja Serbica and started shooting at your tractors, but after the intervention of Serb families, they stopped, and on that occasion, nobody was hurt; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did this group include policemen in black uniforms?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, there were no members in black uniforms in this group, but later on, in early April, the young men were armed and equipped with uniforms, and the pretext was that they were guarding the village, protecting the village from terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that in the house of Idriz Bytyci, you spent a while and in Donja Serbica you spent a month. The police came there all the time but never harmed you, never looked for you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let us be clear one thing. We spent half of that time in Idriz's house and the other half in another house. We stayed in Serbica for nearly a month. It is true that the police came to Serbica and I did not hear of anyone being threatened by the police. Nobody from us who had moved to that village temporarily and nobody from the villagers of that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that the chief of police from Prizren came to Donja Serbica and said to you that you should go to Albania, anyone who is not from Serbica itself should go to Albania. You did not see the man yourself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see him myself. However, two persons, Serbs from Serbica, and one Albanian, spoke with him, and we were told that the order is for you to get ready and by 5.00, the buses will come and escort you to Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You did not hear with your own ears what he -- his exchange with those three men; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The inhabitants of Donja Serbica, who are local residents, who have their houses there, stayed in Donja Serbica regardless of ethnicity; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They stayed for another two weeks, and after these two weeks, they were expelled as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the area of Donja Serbica, there had been Serb forces since the end of March 1999; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the end of March, there were military forces, not police forces, above Serbica village. They were positioned there for three or four days in a row.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In late March, you left Pirana and went to Donja Serbica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Those two villages have two, two and a half kilometres between them, is that approximately the distance?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your village, Pirana, were there any units of the Serb forces from the 24th of March to the 25th of April 1999, more or less all the time? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 24th of March to the beginning of April, there were, but then they left and came back on the 26th of April, but this time there were soldiers and police, mixed together, and before this date, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's precisely what I'm interested in. In that time frame, in that area, was there any KLA presence? In other words, after the Serb forces left the area, did the KLA forces replace them?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say that the offensive started from the area of Donja Serbica, an offensive started against Retimlje, Randobrava and Pirana, around the 25th of April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So Serb forces were attacking the area in which they had been before and which they had left, and there are no longer any Albanian civilians there. Will you agree with me that it's not logical that those forces would attack fields and woods empty of people?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what you're saying, it's not logical, but I didn't see any KLA soldier there and what I saw was that Albanian houses were set on fire on that day, and those who had not been burned earlier, they were burnt as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it then your testimony today that Serb forces launched an offensive against empty Albanian houses?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, I didn't see any at that time, and it was impossible to go to the village on the 25th and 26th in order to verify or confirm what was going on there. It was impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The position of our Defence team is that it was impossible to go there and inasmuch as that is concerned, we agree with you. However, it was impossible in our opinion because of the intensive fighting between the KLA and Serb forces in that area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see any. I did not see who they were fighting with.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Further in your statement you say that six members of one family were killed in Randobrava village. You corrected that later because you said first they were travelling on a tractor and then you said in that convoy there were no tractors, everybody walked. You did not see this incident. Instead, you were told of it by young men from Randobrava, that you later designated as possible members of the KLA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw the bodies in the stream. I was not present when they were killed, but we saw the bodies and they were killed by shelling. While this young man, he was a civilian, and he told me about another person who was killed. He was not a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. If some time is left we'll come back to that. Later on, they were collected by members of the KLA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see who collected the bodies. Maybe they did, but I did not see them. But I would say this: Some young people from Randobrava helped bury those bodies. We also went to Krusha e Mahde and together with this group of young men, we buried the bodies in Krusha e Mahde.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi, in your statement, in the English version, that is page 3, paragraph 9. In the Albanian this is page 3, last paragraph, and in the B/C/S, page 4, first paragraph, you state, "I saw that their bodies were left on the side of the road for four days and later on they were buried by KLA members." Was this erroneously recorded or is that part of your statement correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's have the Albanian version in front of the witness, please, so that we can check precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Maybe I should try to do the underlining bit again and so we can get quick to it. It will now be the sentence that's underlined in blue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Latifi, could you read aloud the sentence which has been underlined in blue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "I saw that the bodies had remained on the sides of the road for four days and later the KLA would bury them."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And read the rest of the paragraph, to the end, the next two sentences.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The surname of the family was Bytyci, the KLA buried the family some place outside Randobrava."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, you've signed that statement and you have confirmed to us after you took the solemn declaration that you checked it over and it's accurate. So what is the position now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I did not recall this case. But the statement I have -- I can't remember this formulation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've actually told us today that you participated in the funeral.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember that this family was killed. It was killed by Serb shelling, and it was in that stream. The whole family was killed. But I don't remember this part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But you remember telling us this morning, just a few minutes ago, that you along with the group of young men, conducted the funeral for these six family members.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But we were all civilians that day. There were two KLA members, of course, but they only took photos of the bodies. Maybe there is some misunderstanding in the translation. The KLA persons took photographs of the bodies, two of them, and the others who buried them, we were civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you saying these photographs were taken at the funeral?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were buried as they were. The people who took the photos left and took the photographs away with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But did they take the photographs where the family were buried?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. At the place where they were killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You see, that makes the last sentence of this very strange. You say, specifically, it's nothing to do with translation, "The KLA buried the family some place outside Randobrava village." These are your words. You've signed them. You've confirmed them in court here today or yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will clarify. Together with the civilians, there were two KLA members, but they took photographs. They had their own cameras.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi, I've just asked you if these photographs were taken at the place where they were being buried and you said no. So what do you mean by the KLA buried the family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know why I said that. Maybe I misspoke. The KLA was present there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Present where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the place where they were killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When did the event exactly take place? When exactly did you meet these two KLA members?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day, in the village of Randobrava.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What day was that? Can you remember? Or at least approximately?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the 29th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The 29th of what month?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: March, March.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore, at that time, in that area, there were KLA members.

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw these two that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But, of course, you cannot exclude the possibility that there were some other members close by; is that correct as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's a question that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question is and I'm asking you whether you would agree with me, is whether or rather that the Serb forces never controlled the entire area, especially the hilly and wooded terrain of that area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During March and April, I said earlier that from the 24th of March until the end of March, they were there. From the 25th of April, they were again in control of the area. But then after that, I don't know how long they stayed because we left for Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also found the body of a male person in the village of Randobrava. When did you find the body?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same day we found the bodies of that family we mentioned earlier. He was in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who assisted you?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A young colleague there. A young man from the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did anyone task you with carrying out such duties?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Every time the KLA would shoot footage or photographs of the graves; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the funeral?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Funeral or graves. It says here KLA members usually took footage or photographs of the bodies and graves.

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps they did, because the two soldiers that were with us that day, they said, "We are filming everything. We are taking photos of everything."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then you continue, by saying that you buried 25 people from Velika Krusa in Donja Retimlje. When did you do that?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was on the 28th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What month, please?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who helped you out then?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this case, I was with a couple of my relatives, and there was one person from Krusha e Mahde.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You do not come from Donja Retimlje. How come you went to Donja Retimlje on the 28th and did that? Could you move freely about the area after the 24th of March 1999?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we could not move freely. We tried to avoid main roads. We went along the stream and valleys, and I went to Reti to look for my sister. That's why I went there. I went to Reti, I went to Randobrava and then I went to Krusha e Mahde. And then I was interested to see what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore, we can agree that the Serb forces did not control the area we are discussing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they couldn't control the whole area. There were some stationed in Pirana, some others in Reti, and I wouldn't say there were too many of these forces, about 50 or 70 of soldiers and policemen. So there, we could go, follow some paths that they could not see us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Have you ever heard of any KLA members being killed in combat and do you know who would bury such people?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We buried these people ourselves, but the KLA also took notes of the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I want to ask you this: Did you know that some KLA members were killed in fighting and who buried them?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were civilians. They were in civilian clothes. I could not say they were KLA members.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. I won't pursue this any further but I wanted to ask you this: When you went to Albania, were you mobilised there?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the Orahovac offensive and I will conclude my examination with that. Are you referring to the period during which the KLA took over Orahovac town?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We just heard the fighting. I don't know who captured what. The large police forces went towards Orahovac. They went there but then they returned. I'm not sure what happened exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Conclude with this topic. When you left Serbica, you didn't leave because you were forcibly driven away. No one used any force.

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No force was used. We had to leave. Our houses were burned. The danger became greater.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to clarify the issue of use of force. If my learned friends from the OTP wish to clarify this further they will have questions for you, but this will conclude my cross-examination. And I would like to thank Your Honours for having allowed me to pursue my line of questioning in spite of the time constraints.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Latifi, you were asked just now about the Orahovac offensive. Remind us of the date of that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember the date, but it was in summer 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And by offensive, you are referring to an offensive by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, an offensive of the Serb police forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What then, in that case, what do you mean by, "The liberation forces went in the direction of Orahovac? They went there but then they returned?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I don't think I said that. I was misquoted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, could you tell us again, then, what you meant to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not see KLA forces going in the direction of Orahovac. It was the police and military forces that went from Prizren in the direction of Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is a comment for the interpreters. I would like that part of the transcript checked, and a note sent to the Trial Chamber explaining whether the use of the word "liberation forces" is accurate.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: After consultation with a colleague in the booth, it is the interpreter's mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is the interpreter able to say what was actually said?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The colleague and I agree that it was said, "Military and police forces."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I nevertheless think it should be further checked, and a written report sent to the Trial Chamber later. Thank you. One other matter, Mr. Latifi. Did you find your sister?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My sister had gone to Mamusha and from Mamusha they had been expelled to Albania. They had walked all the way from Randobrava to Mamusha to Albania, and about this I learned when I went to Albania. I did not know anything about her fate before that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you meet up with her in Albania?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Marcussen?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi, just a few questions to clarify some parts of what has been going on today and yesterday. I'm going to start with something else but could we prepare Exhibit 3D138, please? And the part I'd like to see would be paragraph 3.3 in that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, do we need to see this, Mr. Marcussen? Is this not something we can read for ourselves in light of the submissions that you will make? What is the witness going to be able to do to elucidate our understanding of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I want him just to confirm that what is in that paragraph is consistent with his evidence. Maybe it's clear enough on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You see, that's a leading question in re-examination and that would not normally be appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: We can deal with it in submissions. I'm happy with that if you prefer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We are talking about a sitrep from the KVM, aren't we?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Indeed it was paragraph 3.2 that was dealt with by the witness. But we can deal with it in submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi, you were also shown another document about the killing of Ymer Xhafiqi, and you confirmed that after that killing, a lot of people left from your village. Do you know why people left?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of the panic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think the witness confirmed that the people left the village. That was precisely the issue at stake yesterday. Therefore, I believe my learned friend's question was unfounded as regards yesterday's testimony. Provided we are not talking at cross-purposes. And I don't think we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is the death that ended yesterday -- or the disappearance that ended yesterday's session, started this morning's session; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the witness has said that he does not remember that as a result of that, 60 per cent of the women left the village for one night, women and children left the village. And he's confirmed that today.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe I misunderstood the evidence. I thought the issue was the composition, the percentage, and not whether people had actually left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, nothing to stop you asking a question. It's only the basis on which you ask it must be accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: To your recollection after this particular killing, did people leave your village?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that they left that day. Don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: That's my misunderstanding. You were also asked today about whether you saw the shelling of the mosque on the 24th, and you confirmed you had seen that. What time of the day did this happen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, again, I don't think that's the proper way that question, and I specifically noted that the witness did not see that, and that he saw the results of it the following morning, and that it was damaged, it was blown up by being mined. Just give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I just checked the transcript. I might have taken a wrong note again but -- my understanding was at page 11 and 12, the witness was saying he didn't see the mining of the mosque but he did see the mosque being shot at and then later on the mosque was mined and he didn't actually see that but let me just ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you see any shooting taking place that hit the mosque at any point in time? Did you see that yourself?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: One shell fell on the minaret.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just old on. There is an objection but it's difficult to see what that is. Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, I believe this has been cleared sufficiently by the answers on page 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This on the face of it seems a perfectly reasonable open question but I will look again at page 12 before deciding.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Hold on, Mr. Marcussen, until I finish reading this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Line 7 and line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just please, I know exactly what I'm doing, Mr. Cepic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There is no proper objection to the question you wish to ask about the shelling of the mosques, so please reformulate it and ask it, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi, did you see at any point in time the mosque being shelled? Did you see that for yourself?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw it myself. Only one shell fell that day but whether it came from Serbica or Landovica, I don't know. While then they shot with Pragas from the bridge. But it did not collapse. So a few days later, we learned that it was mined and then also the same night the mosques of Reti, Randobrava and Landovica were also mined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What do you mean by, "They shot from the bridge"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the bridge, the bridge is at the entrance of the village, and Pragas were stationed there. And the minaret is about 40 metres tall so from there they shot at the mosque, at the minaret.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now is this a different occasion from the one where you say you don't know whether it came from Landobrava [phoen] or Serbica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first shell came either from Serbica or Landovica because there was heavy weaponry in Serbica, there was heavy weaponry in Landovica as well, stationed there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So we understand where one shell came from. Now, what do you -- what are you referring to when you say they shot from the bridge? What form of attack was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a Praga. It can move and it is an anti-aircraft.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you're saying that anti-aircraft gunnery was used to shoot at the mosque? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, at the minaret.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And are you also saying it didn't strike the minaret?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The minaret was struck but it did not collapse that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So is your evidence that anti-aircraft fire actually did damage to the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It damaged the mosque partly, but the anti-aircraft gunnery did not make the mosque collapse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: At what time did you see -- at what time of the day did the shelling, the shell that hit the mosque, take place? When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the morning of the 24th of March, around 11.00 -- 10.00 or 11.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just to complete, I wasn't clear either that you were saying that the shell had hit the mosque. Are you saying that the one shell that landed actually hit the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To be more precise, a shell fell in the area between the mosque and the minaret, and then the mosque was being hit by anti-artillery gunnery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is the minaret separate from the mosque building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The building of the mosque is lower but the minaret is thinner and taller and it is close to the mosque building. It is attached to the mosque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So they are physically attached, they are physically attached to each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. They are physically attached in one corner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So when you say a shell landed between the minaret and the mosque, did it hit the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It hit the minaret. It hit the area between the building and the minaret. A part of the mosque was hit as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Marcussen?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Just as a point of reference for the future when this is being looked at, I think what is at issue is the last paragraph on page 2 of the statement where it says that in the morning, at 8.00, a house -- the houses were set on fire, luckily there was no damage to -- no damage or people killed. That's what we are trying to narrow down when this actually took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What has that got to do with the mosque?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think it was being suggested that the witness wasn't consistent in the incident with the mosque because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm wondering why it's not mentioned in relation to that shooting. I mean, is it mentioned in the statement at all? I thought the point was that this destruction of the minaret was not referred to in the statement. We know it came up in another statement but it doesn't appear in this statement. Does it? Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard from you exactly the words I wanted to say, and I'm afraid that my learned friend, Mr. Marcussen, didn't read out paragraph 8 in its totality. At the same time it says simultaneously the Serbs began shelling the village but luckily, there was no damage or people being killed or wounded. This is what literally is stated in this 1999 statement. In the Milosevic transcript, this same witness did not mention the destruction of the minaret. It is not included in this 1999 statement either. And this is the first time we've heard of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, I think I said that before you even opened your mouth, just now, and really we are wasting an awful lot of time now on something that is doubtful that the Trial Chamber is going to pay much attention to in view of its absence from the original statement. Is there any other questions, Mr. Marcussen?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Just one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You were asked by Mr. Lukic about the period of time when the Serb forces had left the area that you were seeking refuge in and then came back and that there was shelling of the villages on the 26th, around the time of the 26th of April. Did you hear any outgoing fire from any of the villages being shelled?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. That concludes our redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi, in what -- what were the circumstances which led to you first mentioning the damage to the minaret to the office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned it by accident. I wasn't asked by members of the Prosecution about this. I mentioned it by accident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was after the Milosevic testimony. I think I've mentioned it to OTP members in Prishtina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Latifi, that completes your evidence. Thank you very much for coming to the Tribunal to give evidence and to expand upon it over the last two days. You are now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, we shall resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Fikirini, who is the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [In English] Your Honour, excuse me. [Interpretation] I did not want to take time away from the break but just in case, I would like to tender a list of documents bearing in mind your observation, I tender 3D134.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If this is simply a reference to the documents which you brought up on the e-court during the evidence, and which set the questions in context, then they are admitted to the extent necessary to understand the evidence. The only reason that the Prosecution on occasions tender documents is when they are, for example, a statement or a transcript, because they are being tendered in their entirety for us to consider in their entirety, but where it's simply a question of referring to a document to put question in context, you don't need to go through that exercise, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Fikirini?

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honour, our next witness is William Fulton. His evidence is relevant to paragraph 75(D) and he will be a live witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon -- good morning, sorry, Mr. Fulton.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you stand, please. And could you make the solemn declaration by reading aloud what's being placed before you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Fikirini?

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honours, before I proceed, I have an issue which I would like to sort out with you. I will have several documents which I'll be using with this witness, and the documents, they all have index pages referring to those documents. My question is: Would you also like me to put on the screen those indexes, pages, or would you like me to just put on the photographs which are relevant to this witness? The witness will be discussing about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So, for example, when you come to P166 --

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- that's an index and P167 is actually --

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: The photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- the document itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It sounds to me as though there is no real reason for going through the index unless it's necessary to identify anything as we go along. So unless that presents a difficulty, I think you should assume we don't need to see the index but we'll note that the related index will be an exhibit in relation to any of the exhibits that are actually referred to as we go through the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Could you please state your full name to the Court?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: William Robert Fulton.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Fulton, are you country working with the United Nations truce supervision organisation in Jerusalem; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And before you joined United Nations truce supervision organisation in Jerusalem, were you a police officer holding the rank of detective sergeant with the police service of Northern Ireland?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And Mr. Fulton, while you were working with the police service of Northern Ireland, did you co-author a contiguous plan on the recovery and identification of dead bodies in major disasters?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I did, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Fulton in September and October 1999, were you seconded to the British forensic team to work in Kosovo and again in 2000 for exhumation work?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Between May 2001 and 2005 you had been working with the Office of the Prosecutor as an investigator; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Fulton, in June 2001, you were assigned to work in the Belgrade field office by team leader then, Mr. Kevin Curtis to monitor the exhumation process that was scheduled to take place within the boundaries of Serbia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: While in that assignment, in total, how many exhumation sites you monitored?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Exclusively, two, and I did have then -- I visited the two further sites on one day at Petrova Selo. I visited a further site at Lake Peruca with the river Derventa on another day but primarily my task was to look after the grave sites that were recovered or discovered in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Can you name the name -- can you name those sites?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: We had two sites in Petrovo Selo, Petrovo Selo 1 and 2. We had a number of sites in Batajnica. My understanding is it eventually went up to 7 or 8. I was certainly there for Batajnica 1, 2 and 3 and we had another site at Lake Peruca.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point I will ask for Exhibit P0063 to be placed on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you mean 631?

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: 631, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Fulton, can you describe to the Court or can you show to us where those sites are located and if possible, can you tell us the distance from Belgrade and whether those mass graves were in the common area or there was any specific thing related to those mass graves?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I recall that the sites in Batajnica were approximately about 20 kilometres from Belgrade. As to the actual distance for Petrovo Selo and Peruca sites I genuinely cannot recall but there was some considerable distance.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And Mr. Fulton, how did you come about this -- I mean, how did you come about the information regarding this mass graves?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: My understanding is that it was clearly there was some press coverage regarding this and it came to the attention of the Office of the Prosecutor, which resulted in my hasty departure from here. After a few days of arriving to go to Belgrade, and that's when it was then brought to my attention, about the initial site in Batajnica. I know there was an

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: police, and as a result of his investigations, it then led to the determining where these grave sites were.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And do you know who ordered and who carried this exhumations?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: The exhumations were carried out exclusively by members of Rade, of forensic institutes within Serbia. I'm trying to recall which one was involved in Petrovo Selo, Uzica perhaps. This was another one in Peruca which carried out under the control of a VJ forensic pathologist and certainly the ones in Batajnica were led by professor Dusan Dunjic of the Belgrade forensic institute.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Fulton, you were asked to monitor the exhumation in Serbia and you mentioned several sites involved. My questions are: Were all identified mass graves at that time exhumed?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And were you present at all these sites?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: The exhumations in for example Petrovo Selo were carried on in tandem to the ones that were going on in Batajnica. The one in -- that's been marked was going -- was also being carried out again. Can't recall exact dates but to such that I was able to visit those other two sites on one day each. The Batajnica site certainly BA 1 and 2 BA I was there exclusively during that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And Mr. Fulton, while you were still with the Office of the Prosecutor, do you remember or were there any time the OTP received reports, records of the exhumation carried out at -- in Batajnica, Petrovo Selo and Lake Peruca?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: From the Serbian authorities?

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes. My understanding is that although I left Belgrade during June, I believe of 2003, I know that there had been requests put in for the complete files from the relevant investigating judges and I have no doubt that they were received here. In fact I know that certainly the first Batajnica files were submitted to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Fulton, I would like to specifically take you to the Batajnica 1 site. With this site, you told us that you were there exclusively. Can you tell us when did it start and when did it end if you remember the exhumation exercise?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I believe it started on 12th of June, and lasted on the 26th, I believe. I know that the Petrovo Selo site was going on after that because I visited it on the 27th of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Now can you just focus on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Mr. Fulton, what do you mean by the expression you were there exclusively?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was my focus and my arrival at the time, sir, was just to be an observer at these exhumations. So I was there primarily -- that was my main task at the time I was supposed to do in an observation capacity on behalf of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Since you are talking about Batajnica 1, I would appreciate if you would focus on that.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Fulton, you earlier told us that these sites were outside Belgrade. With this site specifically, Batajnica 1, can you further explain where it's located within that area?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Within the area of Batajnica, there is a VJ camp. I since found out afterwards that within the VJ camp there was a special anti-terrorist police facility inside that. There is a firing range on one of the boundary walls. Beyond it is where the first site was found, within a matter of metres of the boundary fence.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And you also told the Court just a few minutes ago that you were there as a monitor. Were you -- as an observer. Were you the only one observing this exhumation exercises?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: No, my recollection is that I believe there was a Swiss pathologist there. There was members of the ICMP, HRC were also there. There were quite a number of observers.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: What do you mean by ICMP, HRC?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: International Commission for Missing Persons and Human Rights Commission, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And based on your role, did you collect or receive any information regarding the exhumations in Batajnica 1?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: With regard to identification documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: No. Just out of that exhumation, did you receive any reports or the OTP did receive any reports, any photographs, any documents?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes. My understanding is that once the complete forensic report was submitted to the Belgrade district court, a copy of this was then forwarded to the Office of the Prosecutor by the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point I would ask Exhibit P00159 to be placed on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Fulton, can you explain or describe to the Court what these photographs depict?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That's a scene of the exhumation site from BA 01, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: That's when the exhumation started?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Well, I can't be specific if that is one of the photographs regarding the start of it but yes, it certainly looks like it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And do you know who was taking these pictures?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: There was a criminal technician from the Serbian MUP who was tasked there as a -- to technically record what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And Mr. Fulton, were there any bodies exhumed or recovered from this site and if yes, how many?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: What was passed to me, I believe, was there was at least 37 bodies that were recovered from this particular grave site.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Fulton, were you able to see in what state the bodies exhumed were?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There was basically a pile of co-mingled bodies, bones, flesh, clothing, in a -- I don't know, a mass heap in the middle of this site.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And were you able to get any information as to the bodies exhumed, the identification documents recovered, including loose clothings?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes. Whenever bodies were recovered or clothe -- each item of clothing or things that were found were evidentially recorded by the forensic team. If there was an identification document or something of specific interest, this was brought to our attention and these details were then passed to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And Mr. Fulton, from the bodies exhumed and the artifacts recovered, was there any matching between the bodies and the identification document recovered done?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: At this stage there was no identifications done, Your Honour. These were identification documents that were recovered, either they were found loose or they were found in items of clothing that were loose or they were found on items of clothing that were on bodies or body parts.
