This was not about identification. It was simply that I recorded that these documents were identification documents that were recovered from the site.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: What about the presumptive identification based on how the documents were found in relation to the bodies exhumed? Did such a thing happen?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: A presumptive identification is -- what we had here were identification documents. At no point did myself or anybody at that time -- because the identification requires the linking of anti-mortem data to post-mortem data. These identification documents were certainly indicative of something but beyond that I'm not in a position then or now to say that they presumed identification of any of the bodies that we recovered there.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Now, based on that indications, were there any identification done based on -- I mean, on the documents which were found and what you are calling now as indicative, did anything happen?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: As a result of the documents --

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: -- being found? No, because it's simply insufficient. I mean clearly they indicate certain things but it's insufficient for the -- for -- for the definitive identification of a body based on some documents that were recovered from a mass grave site.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: From these specific sites, did you receive any photographs, any identification documents?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I believe so, yes, sir. They were handed over, a complete file regarding the exhumation process and the forensic reports were handed over from the forensic institute to the investigating judge. And as a result of that they became -- they came into the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this stage I would ask if Exhibit P00139 could be placed on the screen. Mr. Fulton, do you have any recollection as to some of these photographs which were passed on to you and then you passed them to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I do have some recollection of them, not each specific photograph obviously, but yes this looks like I can see the identification moniker that was given to this grave site as being BA.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And can you describe to the Court what this photograph which is in front of you depicts?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: The working -- again I don't want to speak on behalf of the forensic team involved, but the practice was whenever there was what was deemed to be either a definitive body or body part or something of significance was initially identified, they evidentially recorded it prior to the exhumation, the exhumation itself, and then the body after it was exhumed. This is when a body or a body part of significance was identified and they would have placed the markers in the ground evidentially recorded it and then carried on with their exhumation process.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Can we move to the second page of these photographs, please? Can you describe to the Court also what is on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Although the photographs now make it appear quite indistinct but clearly at the time, they would have identified body BA 09 and BA 010 so they marked their location, they plotted it by way of taking photographs.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Can we go to the next photograph, please? Mr. Fulton, would the Registry, please, I mean, keep on putting different photographs so that the witness can continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I ask what the purpose of this exercise is? Is there not a report that links these photographs and the contents of the photographs and any other material and tells us what the outcome of the investigation was?

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honour, with a different witness, yes, we will be able to achieve what you think should be done, but with this specific witness, no, because he didn't put any report together. His task was to observe what was happening at the exhumation sites and this is the information which was collected and specifically to this site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And will the witness to whom you refer not be able to deal with all this? I wasn't expecting him to deal with all of this specifically knowing that this is that, but these are the photographs which were sent to him as he was there at the exhumation site. So this is the product of what he was observing while he was at the exhumation site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All this witness is saying is, yes, that looks like a photograph that was taken at Batajnica because I'm familiar with the general layout of the exhumation site. He's not said any -- is he going to be saying more than that about any of the other photographs?

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: He won't be able to say exactly what because his task wasn't -- he wasn't there to say anything or to make any remarks. He was just there to observe the whole process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, do we need this evidence? It doesn't sound like it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we need because there is a question of these bodies moved from one point to another. There is a question of these mass graves. There is a question of how these bodies were while they were in the graves, so I think we need that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And he's going to tell us these things, is he?

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Yes. I mean he won't tell us that the bodies were moved but he will tell us what was at the exhumation sites. How did --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But we are going to have a report that tells us what's in each of these photographs by the people who really did the work presumably. So why do we need him to go through the photographs and say, yeah, this looks like what I saw at the time, but I can't say any more than that? Maybe I'm missing something. I'd like you to alert me to what it is you think I'm missing that this evidence might establish?

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honour, it cuts both ways. You might not be missing anything, but you might also be missing something. He was sent by the OTP to observe what was taking place, and out of his observation or his presence at the exhumation site, resulted in us or the OTP getting this information. There are other people who were there, like the forensic experts, of course we will call them, they will also give us their piece of evidence of what happened and how they carried out that exercise. But his work or why he was there, he was there as an observer on behalf of the OTP and based on that, we thought it it's very important for him also to come as a witness so that he can share his piece of evidence on what he observed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Who is the witness that will come and deal with the matter in detail? And speak to a report?

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: We have two forensic experts. We'll have an archeologist who was present at some of these sites and who put together a report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And who are the two forensic pathologist?

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: We have Professor Dunjic and we have Professor Alexandric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And are they the two who were mentioned earlier in Mr. Fulton's evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: He mentioned one of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And he said another was a VJ pathologist; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Yes, but again, we are not going to specifically deal with Lake Peruca, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan, can you help me on this? This -- the 65 ter summary indicates a list of names of persons and it would appear that it's suggested that these are people killed elsewhere and whose bodies were found at Batajnica. Now, is there an issue over the identification of these people in this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: That's an issue that I alone cannot speak to. I think you'd have to canvass the position of the other accused, their council.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you have a position on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: We hold the Prosecution to strict proof of identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We are being realistic, are we, on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Well, before the Prosecution say they intend to call a number of witnesses in connection with that and I can -- questions you've been putting to the Prosecution in relation to this witness. The position that or the questions you are asking at this point in this testimony are questions that I'm asking myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: As far as you're concerned, though, is it beyond the realms of possibility that the fact that certain bodies were probably killed in one place and later found in a quite separate place might be agreed?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: That's a matter I cannot speak to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Obviously, it doesn't prove how they got there, which may be the most important factor of all, although certain inferences might be drawn from that, but I wonder if this is something to which attention might have been given. If I'm told by the Defence it's out of the question, then of course, that's the end of the matter. But perhaps I should ask the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Perhaps give an opportunity to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You sound ambivalent at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: It shows we haven't fully discussed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps I could assist some. As I think the witness has already testified, the matters which he observed and which he has knowledge of cannot forensically and conclusively speaking identify the remains. There was an investigation carried out, and again I don't want to be testifying but it's my understanding that DNA testing was undertaken on certain of these remains that results were found and therefore the forensic experts ought to be able to talk about their investigation and results and I believe indeed the investigations conducted by the investigating judge and by the working group of the MUP have -- will be heard here and that evidence will speak for itself, and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you -- I understand what you're saying so far, but are you also saying that there is just no question of reaching agreement on this evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm not. I think there is a possibility of reaching agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does it not feature in the document that's circulating or has been circulating trying to encourage agreement among you?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't believe that was one of the items that was sought to be agreed on, to be quite frank, Your Honour, but I do know that and in fact I believe this witness testified about during the time that this witness testified in Milosevic, the DNA results were still pending and since that time, certain DNA results have come back so with respect to certain of the unidentified bodies, I believe forensically speaking the proper officials can make an identification now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, thank you, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Fikirini, we will allow to you proceed for the moment, but certainly my impression is that this evidence isn't actually going to assist us greatly. We have been assisted so far by looking at what the site was like, hearing the description from Mr. Fulton of what he saw when the site was initially opened up, and that's useful, helpful and it's in the public interest that that should be heard, but I wonder if it really is in the public interest to go through with him all these photographs which other witnesses are going to be better able to speak about. But if you want to carry on and take us to areas you think he can help us with we'll listen a little longer and see if it is going to be productive.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you for that. I will agree with the Chamber that probably for him to go through all these documents will not be very helpful, but for being -- for him being here it's very important because there are two areas which he will touch which the other witnesses who will be coming later won't be touching, and I was trying to lay a foundation before getting to that point. There are two specific things: One, it's the document -- documents which were found next to the bodies or in the clothings which were on the bodies exhumed, and those documents which they were brought over to the OTP. The OTP was able to match those victims who were on our schedule to the documents which were recovered and basically, he is the only witness who could speak about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: He's not too happy about that taking us anywhere, though. But you're welcome to continue to ask him about the matter, if you feel that that's the only way that that link can be made.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Fulton, when you were at the exhumation site and after receiving the documents from the Belgrade court, and those documents were brought over to the OTP, was there any time those documents were matched to the victims who are on our schedules? For example, schedule D, which is victim from Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. A number of the documents that were recovered matched some of the details of the victims who were involved in the Suva Reka, and again they were an indicator and what they did was simply -- in those early days as has been previously pointed out, and with regard to the Milosevic trial, they were indications because the DNA hadn't yet been established and clearly things have moved on from then, but they did provide an indication of where the bodies may have come from.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I would like just to quickly go through the names at least of those people who are on our schedule D. Can we can go back --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the purpose of that Ms. Fikirini?

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: At least -- I know it might be very difficult to connect this but one of the witnesses or some of the witnesses from Suva Reka did testify before this Court that some of the victims who were killed were buried at the firing range. Some of these bodies were later found in Batajnica. There is our evidence. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Any way, continue with the questions so I hear what it actually amounts to.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: With the question to the witness or my explanation to the Court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Can we then go back to Exhibit P0039 and can the Registry please scroll to where they will come across --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think that's 139.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: 139. Where they will come across a licna karta. This is the identification document which will give us a light as to the importance of this witness before this Court. Okay. Let us stop there.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Fulton, is this one of many documents which were found at Batajnica which relate or were an indication?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As we can see it's after Berisha. It was then brought to may attention that this was one of the potential victims or persons that were killed at Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And from that site, how many bodies or how many documents you found which relate to that?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I didn't find any of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: I mean how many documents you received?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Nor --

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: At least the licna kartas which were given clue or which were indications that these people were from Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I believe there was eight identification documents recovered. I didn't -- I was never in receipt of these documents. I was in receipt of the details that were contained within these documents as recovered by the forensic team. Again, the linkage that was made between the document found and the deaths that occurred at Suva Reka were carried out in this office, not in Belgrade, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if we could take a break? Five minutes? --- Break taken at 11.45 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, bring the witness in, please. Ms. Fikirini, are you feeling comfortable enough to carry on?

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If there is any difficulty and you need another break, please let me know.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for your concern and I'm sorry for the interruption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Not at all. Carry on now.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Fulton, before this break, I asked you if there were any licna kartas or identification documents which were recovered from this site which in a way give a clue that some of these documents found relate to the victims on schedule D to the third amended indictment.

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Basically what they did give an indication of where the victims may have come from. It is fair to say that events had happened after that was whenever there was a clearly the need for something more than physical or clothing identification, to try and identify where the bodies came from. This then would have led the OTP and other organisation in a particular direction where they would obtain blood samples for DNA analysis and that's what happened to the best of my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And from the work which you or the exhumation which you observed at Batajnica 1, was there any time you accompanied Mr. -- Sorry, Professor Dunjic to Madrid?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes. I mean the samples were always -- the ownership was always under the forensic institute and the Serbian authorities. I accompanied them to Madrid purely as a facilitator more than anything else. There had been again to my recollection some considerable negotiations and establishing that there was no facility in Serbia where they were in a position to carry out DNA analysis and as a result, the institute in Madrid offered their services and that resulted in our travel to Madrid.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like now to move to Batajnica 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Fulton, you told us that you were at Batajnica 1 and Batajnica 2 full time. Do you remember, if you do, when did it start and when did it end?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I believe it started on the 10th of July 2001 and lasted until September.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And were there any bodies recovered from that site?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Again my recollection there was at least 269 bodies recovered from that site, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And were there any identification documents also recovered from that site?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, there was, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Was all -- I mean, was there any point when this information regarding the documents recovered and the number of bodies exhumed passed on to you and then you passed that information to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: It was exactly the same procedure. Whenever something of significance was recovered with regard to identification documents, it was brought to my attention and I then passed it on to this office.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Do you by any chance remember how many identification documents were recovered from this site, were passed on to you?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I believe there was 11 items of potential identification, although one of them was a dog tag, it was described to me as a dog tag, but there were a number of document that did relate to persons that had been listed as being killed in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And was there any time you learned that probably the information which you passed on to the OTP, the OTP was able to match that information with the name of the victims appearing on schedule I to the third amended indictment?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I know that as a result of some of the documents, you can see in this case it's still on screen, some of the information that was contained in the documents, it is fair to say that some of the documentation was better than others due to either burning or purely degradation as a result of their time in the ground. And as a result of the information recovered from that they were then checked with the ICRC book on missing persons and as a result of that, they were able to say that the details recovered from this particular grave site could well have been persons who were listed as missing in the ICRC document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point I will move to the third site which is Petrovo Selo 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Fulton, you said you were present at this site for a day or two; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I was there for one day, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: One day. And was there any body exhumed from this site?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, there was two sites. It is fair to say that I'm aware that there was an ICMP registered monitor there for the best part of that and I understand that he's also submitted his report on that. My recollection is that Petrovo Selo, ten, 17 bodies. I can't -- no, maybe ten bodies. I just can't remember, but I know that in Petrovo Selo there were 59 bodies recovered, I think or at least that number.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Again, were there any identification documents recovered too?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I do recall that there was it was indicated to me that there was a number of documents recovered from the first side and they referred specifically to three brothers by the name of Bitici. I remember at the time they were American citizens, as it transpired, from Chicago, and their last known as was indicated to me, their last known place were they were imprisoned in Nis, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Were they the only bodies recovered or were there other bodies recovered?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: No, no. There were other bodies recovered, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Okay. This is from Petrovo Selo 2 or still 1?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That was the Bitici's were from 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And from Petrovo Selo 2?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I understand there were some other documents recovered although I have no recollection of the numbers or from where they referred to at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, moving to Lake Peruca, how long were you there or were you there to monitor these exhumations?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Again, I visited it for -- number of other -- it's right on the western border with Bosnia quite close to Bajina Basta, so I was actually on site for one day, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And did you learn from those who were working there and are taking the exhumations if there were any bodies exhumed?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, there was indications that there would be at least the bodies of 48 people had been recovered. I should say to the Court, I said at least because in those days it was -- it was indistinct the number of bodies and it was -- it takes further examination by the forensic teams. I have no doubt it's simply been clarified at this point by the forensic reports that have been submitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And were there also identification documents which were recovered from that site?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: My recollection is that there was two identification documents recovered.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you give us the date when you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember it vividly because I was there on site on the 11th of September 2001, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And the other three sites were all in the same year -- you've given us the dates already, they are all 2001?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. Although I understand that the exhumations in Batajnica within the SAJ firing range continued through 2002 as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, what, then, is the position in relation to the various exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Since we haven't worked with this witness on these exhibits, I don't see any reason of asking the Court for these exhibits to be admitted at this point. I will wait until the other witnesses come because most of them will be referred to by Professor Dunjic and Professor Alexandric and an archeologist from ICMP. So I think that will be the convenient or the proper time for me to submit them to court as exhibits and not with this witness, since we haven't really used them with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The Chamber has had an opportunity to briefly discuss the position while we had that break, and we recognise that it's important to recognise victims of a conflict, and it may be important to the presentation of your case that that is done. However, it does seem to us that there is potential for agreement on this material. Now, potential is putting it obviously at its highest but the response when the matter was raised earlier was not to reject the idea. Mr. O'Sullivan in saying that obviously if they insist, the Defence can put the Prosecution to their full proof, he nevertheless sounded somewhat ambivalent on the matter and therefore it does appear to us that agreement is at least worth exploring. And in the course of exploring it, if you do manage to reach agreement on the identification of certain victims, then that could be presented to us in a written form that can also be publicly acknowledged. It's not a matter that necessarily needs to take up in-court time, if there is room for agreement. Bearing in mind the limited time available and the many issues that have to be explored. So we encourage you to endeavour to reach agreement on at least some of this material that might reduce the time that has to be spent on the detail which may turn out to be non-controversial.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Fikirini.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: -- for the advice. And the Prosecution will definitely work on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. O'Sullivan?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the order will be General Lukic, General Pavkovic, General Lazarevic, Mr. Milutinovic, Mr. Sainovic and General Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I should be fairly brief. I don't have that many questions. I have about a dozen questions.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You want to complete your cross-examination before the break, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can try, Your Honour. I've got about five or six questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You should carry on and then if we can break about half past if you haven't finished by then.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'll try to and finish Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Now, sir, did it appear to you -- strike that. Am I correct that the investigative authorities for the exhumations secured the sites and in fact waited to begin their work to permit sufficient notice to the OTP so that the OTP could send one of its representatives to observe every facet of the exhumation?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I can only assume that that was the case, Your Honour. It seemed to be that way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And are you aware that the exhumation itself was being conducted under the auspices and under the control of two investigative judges, one for Batajnica 1 and one for Batajnica 2?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm very well aware of that, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And am I correct that the Serbian MUP provided security throughout the exhumation process for the site as well as for the exhumation teams?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: Yes, that is also correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And now, as far as the cause of death for any of the victims that were exhumed, am I correct you would have to defer to the expertise of the forensic pathologists that undertook the forensic portion of that investigation?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: That would be the case, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And as for the criminal culpability of anyone arising out of those events, you would have to defer to the competent authorities that undertook the investigation for that regard as well?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I would, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Okay. And is it correct or do you have knowledge that the Serbian MUP authorities even before the official DNA results came back from Madrid, that they worked based upon the informal indications of where the corpses came from, to commence investigations already at that time, and to try to ascertain the manner of death and those responsible for the same?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I would have to assume that that was the case, Your Honour. It would be a foolish practice not to take cognizance of the documents that were recovered at those scenes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much, Mr. Fulton. I believe I'm completed with this witness. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Aleksic, do you have questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have any questions either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honour, there may be a question or two.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Fulton, you were asked if the OTP did receive all the documents or all the records and information from the Serbian authorities in relation to these exhumations and the bodies exhumed. Was this a one-time thing or was it an ongoing thing?

utterances.speaker: WILLIAM ROBERT FULTON
utterances.text: I'm fully aware that certainly from the Batajnica 1 site, it was handed in by Judge Goran Cavlina and I know that there has been ongoing contact with Judge Milan Dilparic regarding the other sites in Batajnica. I do believe that all requests for the information with regard to the forensic exhumation of the bodies has been received at the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Fikirini.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. The transcript records your last answer as saying all requests for information with regard to the forensic exhumations of the bodies has been received at the Office of the Prosecutor. Do you extend that to the forensic examination?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it was a complete package, Your Honour that showed the exhumation process and the procedures that they -- with regard to determining death and ultimately identification if it was relevant, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, thank you, Mr. Fulton. That completes your evidence. Thank you again for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You're now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before you rise, Your Honours, we have a difficulty. The witness could leave. It doesn't relate to the evidence. We have been moving pretty quickly and we are bringing forward witnesses that were scheduled for next week to cover this week. We are now having a difficulty in having a witness on this afternoon. I think the witness arrived recently and is still being proofed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You have two witnesses more scheduled for this week but one of them could be for more than a day; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: A great deal depends on the length of the cross-examination. With respect to one of them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I thought they anticipated examination-in-chief was four hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, but we have in our filing recently - I can't recall the date - indicated that we would like to take him on a 92 ter as he has already testified with some live -- with the leave of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: To ask him a few questions. I don't anticipate we will be going, certainly not as much as four hours in chief, much less than that, as a matter of fact. So I don't think there would be much lost this week but we are really in a difficulty for this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Having regard to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- that's a euphemism, I take it, for having no witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is a correct interpretation of what I was saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, if you don't have a witness, there is not a lot we can do, is there? Is there an issue over -- well, can we briefly again go back to private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, during the evidence -- just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you intending to deal with the same matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, something completely different, a technical issue.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, during the evidence of yesterday's witness Ndrec Konaj, I tendered the transcript of that witness's testimony from the Milosevic trial, and I gave you an indication, 3D129, for that transcript. However, for technical reason, the correct identification would be 3D143. And I would like that to be on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic. That clarifies the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We will adjourn now and resume at 9.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 18th day of October, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.
